family: collect/expand counter with drains; growth cycle
summary: Two blocks trade places, about 7 times longer each round, until the left one is drained into the block at the right end; from step 1.8·1015 on the run repeats exactly every 116,320,154 visits of the left end with the right block 321,042,928 words longer, so it never halts. Proved in Lean: a symbolic executor with a soundness proof replays the arrival and one period for every odd length (compiled evaluation, native_decide).
title: What is known about 1RB0RC_0RC1RC_0LD0RA_1LE0LF_0LA1LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_0RC1RC_0LD0RA_1LE0LF_0LA1LC_---1LA.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It does not halt when started on a blank tape; the proof is in Lean, with its two long computations evaluated by compiled code. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: It does not halt (Lean theorem nonhalt, level native). From step 1,818,198,163,340,705 on, the configuration E> 0 (1011001)^59 1011 00000 1101100110110 (011)^16 001101100110 (011)^r comes back with r larger by 321,042,928 after 116,320,154 arrivals at the left end, for every odd r ≥ 65. In Lean, a symbolic executor whose every move is proved to be a run of the machine (kernel) replays the arrival from blank tape and one period with r = 65 + 2x, x free; the two replays and the twelve cycle rules they use are evaluated by native_decide, so the result rests on the Lean kernel and the Lean compiler. The exact step and visit counts are computed by the Python and C++ simulators (trusted), not part of the Lean statement.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 43,491 cells have been visited and 26,502 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478).

claims.title: Sweeps over the long blocks
claims.text: L A>(0011011)^n R → L (1100110)^n A> R (13n steps), L (1011001)^n D>1 R → L D>1 (0110110)^n R (23n steps), L A>(011)^n R → L (110)^n A> R (3n steps), for every n, L, R.

claims.title: The two long phases, any number of cycles
claims.text: Collecting: E> 0 (1011001)^p (101)^5 10 (011)^q 000 (011)^r (q even, r odd) becomes the same with p + 2n, q − 2n. Expanding: E> 0 (1011001)^p 1011 0^5 110110011010 (101)^m 1000 (011)^r (m even, r odd) becomes the same with p − 2n, m + 14n. One cycle each with its exact step count (48a + 48b + 72p + 476 and 240b + 240c + 144p + 2812), n cycles by induction.

claims.title: The machine does not halt
claims.text: From blank tape the machine never reaches a halting configuration: nonhalt : ¬ HaltsFromBlank. It combines the three claims below with nonhalting_of_growth_cycle. Axioms used: propext, Quot.sound and 14 compiled evaluations (native_decide): the two replays and the twelve cycle rules.

claims.title: The machine does not halt: a second proof, in Coq (busycoq)
claims.text: The same argument, ported to Coq on top of busycoq's definitions: nonhalt : ~ halts tm c0. The symbolic executor is proved sound against busycoq's step, and all runs are evaluated inside Coq's kernel by vm_compute; Print Assumptions nonhalt reports no axioms. Clean build with Coq 8.18.0: about 40 s.

claims.title: A growth cycle implies non-halting
claims.text: With C(r) = E> 0 (1011001)^59 1011 00000 1101100110110 (011)^16 001101100110 (011)^r: if the run from blank tape reaches some C(65 + 2x), and every C(65 + 2x) reaches C(65 + 2(x + 160,521,464)) in at least one step, the machine does not halt from blank tape. The two hypotheses are proved by the replay below.

claims.title: A symbolic executor, proved sound
claims.text: Tapes are lists of cells and blocks (w)^n with n = c + a0x0 + a1x1 + …, the x free. A move is a shift rule from a table (a block crossed at once, one or two copies at a time), or one machine step, and at each arrival of state E at the left end a re-bracketing of the tape and a cycle rule applied N times at once. Any step that would depend on a variable fails. Theorem: if the executor goes from S to S′ in k moves and its tables are valid, the machine goes from S to S′ for every value of the variables. The 31 shift rules are proved by evaluation in the kernel; the N-fold application of a cycle rule by induction.

claims.title: Twelve cycle rules, for all values of their counts
claims.text: Each rule says: this tape with counts bi + 2xi comes back with counts bi + Di + 2xi, for all xi (eleven are collect or expand, plain or with inert zones in between, 2 or 4 visits; one is the drain, 72 visits, 201,007 executor moves). Each is one run of the executor without cycle rules, evaluated by native_decide.

claims.title: Blank tape reaches C(16,797,709)
claims.text: 5,037,044 moves of the executor from blank tape end at C(16,797,709) (arrive_run, native_decide, 13 s); by soundness the machine reaches that configuration.

claims.title: C(65 + 2x) reaches C(65 + 2(x + 160,521,464)), for every x
claims.text: 5,581,714 moves of the executor from C(65 + 2x), x a free variable, end at C(321,042,993 + 2x) (period_run, native_decide, 14 s); by soundness the machine does so for every x, in at least one step.

claims.title: The growth cycle: visit and step counts
claims.text: C(r) reaches C(r + 321,042,928) after 116,320,154 arrivals at the left end and 650,373,336,347,246,654 + 4,382,930,856 (r − 65) steps. That C(r) reaches C(r + 321,042,928) is a Lean theorem (above); the counts come from two symbolic simulators that agree (py/closure/accel.py and the model of the Lean executor, py/replay/engine.py), checked against numeric runs from C(65), C(67), C(79) and three periods of the real run; 17 injected defects are all reported.

claims.title: Blank tape reaches the cycle: step counts
claims.text: That blank tape reaches C(16,797,709) is a Lean theorem (above). The step counts are computed: the run is at C(16,797,709) after 1,818,198,163,340,705 steps (event 6,086,451), and at C(337,840,637) after 725,814,446,706,290,623 steps. The word-level engine agrees with a plain C simulator at all 24,646 events of the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps (step count and CRC of the tape).

claims.title: Neighbouring classes halt
claims.text: The same pattern with 61 words in the left block halts for every odd r ≥ 65, after 1,772,276 + 5,220 (r − 65) steps (confirmed by plain simulation for r = 65, 67, 71); C(r) with r even ≥ 64 halts at its 21,362,421st event. So the real run is safe only because of the exact orbit it is on.

claims.title: Independent check of the growth cycle
claims.text: A second accelerated simulator, written from scratch without reading the first (verify/sim3.cpp, validated against plain simulation to 1010 steps), lands exactly on C(16,797,709) at step 1,818,198,163,340,705 from blank tape, and takes C(r) exactly to C(r + 321,042,928) at the predicted step for r = 65, 67, …, 85 and r = 16,797,709. It also confirms that C(r) halts for the even r tried (the halting transition is one step after the count stated in the notes: that count excludes the halting step). It checks listed values only; “for every odd r” is the Lean theorem grow_cyc.

explainer.lede: It never halts, and Lean proves it. Two blocks of the tape trade places, about seven times longer each round; now and then the left block is poured into a third block at the far right. After 1.8·10<sup>15</sup> steps the whole pattern repeats exactly, with only that third block longer each time.

facts.text: Lean theorem nonhalt; two replays and twelve rules evaluated by compiled code.
The symbolic executor that does the replays is proved sound in Lean.
From step 1.8·10<sup>15</sup> the run repeats every 116,320,154 visits of the left end, the right block 321,042,928 words longer (the counts are computed, the return is proved).
The last step of the argument, proved in Lean.
Injected defects reported by the cycle checker.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478).
After 109 steps the tape spans 43,491 cells (12,594 left of the start, 17,410 right), with a density of 1s of 0.609.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Seven-cell words on the left, three-cell words on the right
html: Look at the tape each time the head, in state E, reaches the left end. It is a block of seven-cell words 1011001, a short irregular zone, and then blocks of the three-cell word 011 separated by a few zeros. The last block, (011)^r, ends the tape.

Going right, the head shifts a block of three-cell words by one cell. Going left, it crosses two words at a time. So what happens at the end of a block depends only on whether its length is even or odd: every rule found has the form “for all lengths of this parity”.

sections.heading: Collect, expand, drain
html: Three regular phases take almost all the time. p counts the seven-cell words, q or m the three-cell words of the middle block, r those of the last block.

phasetape when state E reaches the left endone cycle
collect0 (1011001)^p (101)^5 10 (011)^q 000 (011)^r2 visits: p + 2, q − 2
expand0 (1011001)^p 1011 0^5 110110011010 (101)^m 1000 (011)^r4 visits: p − 2, m + 14
drain0 (1011001)^p 1011 0^5 1101100110110 (011)^16 001101100110 (011)^r72 visits: p − 52, r + 414

Collecting turns three-cell words into seven-cell words one for one; expanding gives seven three-cell words back for each seven-cell word. So each round the blocks are about seven times longer: about 600, 4,370, 30,750, 215,000, 1,506,000 words. Collect and expand are proved in Lean for any number of cycles, by hand and again, with the drain, by the executor.

Between the phases there are short irregular stretches where the separators collide. Usually the next round starts. Sometimes the stretch ends in the drain pattern: then the whole left block is poured into the last block (414 words for 52), and the left part starts again from a small state, in front of a much longer last block.

sections.heading: The left part comes back to the same state
html:
The left part of the tape never needs more of the last block than the parity of its length, and a drain adds an even number of words. After the second drain the left part reaches a state that it meets again, exactly, two drains later:

E> 0 (1011001)^59 1011 00000 1101100110110 (011)^16 001101100110 (011)^r

first with r = 16,797,709 (step 1,818,198,163,340,705), then with r = 337,840,637 (step 725,814,446,706,290,623), then 658,883,565, and so on: 321,042,928 more each time, 116,320,154 visits of the left end apart.

To prove that this goes on for ever, one period is run with r replaced by 65 + 2x, x unknown. Whenever a step would depend on the value of x the run stops; it never had to. It ends in the same configuration with 65 + 321,042,928 + 2x. So every odd r ≥ 65 leads to a larger odd r, and no halting step occurs on the way. A configuration that keeps coming back, larger, never halts.

All of this is a Lean proof. The program that runs the period (a symbolic executor: it moves over whole blocks at once and applies a proved cycle many times in one go) is written in Lean and proved correct once: whatever it does, the machine does, for every x. Lean then runs it: 5.0 million moves from blank tape to the first C(r), 5.6 million moves for one period. Those two runs are done by compiled code (native_decide), which is the one thing trusted beyond Lean's kernel. The exact step counts quoted above come from separate simulators, which agree with each other and with a plain simulator on the first 1010 steps.

sections.heading: Almost the same tape halts
html: With 61 words instead of 59 in the left block, the same pattern halts after about 1.8 million steps, for every odd r. With r even instead of odd, it halts too, much later. Tapes of the same general shape with other counts halt in a few percent of random trials.

So there is no simple description of “safe tapes” that contains the run: it is safe because it sits on one exact orbit. That is why the automatic deciders, which look for such descriptions, left this machine open, and why the proof follows the orbit itself.
